title: Cache-Line Contention and Atomic Synchronization in a Lock-Free Memory-Pool Block Allocator with Embedded Free List (C)
topic: Memory Pool Block Allocator with Free List

abstract: Dynamic memory management in high-concurrency workloads is often limited by cache-line traffic and synchronization overhead. This work presents a lock-free memory-pool block allocator that embeds a singly-linked free list directly inside each block and uses atomic compare-and-swap (CAS) primitives to mediate concurrent acquire and release. The design guarantees that the invariant \textit{used + free = capacity} holds under sequential consistency, and that each operation is linearizable. Empirical evaluation on a Microsoft Azure virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 (96-core) host processor (1 physical core / 2 logical threads, 7.8 GB RAM) under Linux shows a mean allocation latency of \textbf{492.32 \textmu{}s} ($\sigma$ = 39.63 \textmu{}s) and a sustained throughput of \textbf{2,031,185 ops/s} over 30 benchmark iterations. These results demonstrate that the allocator achieves predictable performance despite contention on a shared free-list pointer. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/c-lowlevel-systems/tree/main/algorithms/20261010_160203_memory_pool_block_allocator_wi}
